title: Human History Tour
description: An animated, scroll-driven tour through ~7 million years of human history.

chapters.title: Deep Prehistory & Human Origins
chapters.hook: We stood up long before we grew clever — bipedalism, fire, and stone tools accrued over millions of years, and for this entire span it is an African story with the Americas and Australia still empty.

chapters.title: Paleolithic & the Cognitive Revolution
chapters.hook: For nine-tenths of our history being human meant sharing the planet with other humans — and the oldest painted animal we have found is a wild pig on a Sulawesi cave wall, not a European bison.

chapters.title: The Neolithic Revolution
chapters.hook: Farming was invented not once but at least a dozen times by peoples who never met — a bargain that bought more food and more people at the price of labour, crowd disease, and the hardening of inequality.

chapters.title: First Civilizations & the Bronze Age
chapters.hook: In two dozen centuries humans invented the city, writing, law, and empire on four continents at once — then watched the first globalized world shatter in the Late Bronze Age Collapse.

chapters.title: Classical Antiquity & the Iron Age
chapters.hook: Cheap iron, a learnable alphabet, and coined money rebuilt the world, and from the Aegean to the Ganges to the Yellow River sages independently asked what a good life and a just society are.

chapters.title: The Post-Classical / Medieval World
chapters.hook: The so-called Dark Age was the golden age of Baghdad, Kaifeng, and Angkor — until the very trade roads that carried paper and algebra also carried the Black Death.

chapters.title: The Early Modern Age
chapters.hook: Iberian ships stitched the hemispheres into one entangled world, as silver, print, and gunpowder built the first global economy atop the Columbian Exchange and the transatlantic slave trade.

chapters.title: The Industrial & Modern Age
chapters.hook: In under two centuries humanity harnessed fossil energy and rights-of-man revolutions — closing with the deadliest wars ever fought and a weapon that put civilization's survival in human hands.

chapters.title: The Contemporary & Information Age
chapters.hook: One human lifetime from the first nuclear flash to machines that hold conversations — the age of acceleration, written as much in Delhi, Accra, and Shenzhen as in Washington and Moscow.
